title: One Percent Failure Repeated
problem: A system independently succeeds on each run with probability 0.99. Estimate, without a calculator, the probability that all 100 runs succeed. Give a useful approximation and explain its direction of error.

hints.text: The exact probability is 0.99^100; compare it with e^{-1}.
Since ln(1-0.01) is slightly less than -0.01, 0.99^100 is slightly below e^{-1}.

solution.reasoning: Using ln(1-x)≈-x-x²/2 gives 100 ln(0.99)≈-1.005. Thus the probability is about e^{-1.005}, slightly below e^{-1}≈0.368, or about 0.366.
solution.sanityCheck: The expected number of failures is one, so a no-failure probability near e^{-1} is the standard rare-event benchmark.

keyInsight: Many independent small failure risks naturally produce exponential approximations.
recognitionCues: A probability near one raised to a large power suggests logarithms or the approximation (1-x)^n≈e^{-nx}.
commonMistakes: Answering zero because a failure is expected once on average; expectation does not imply certainty.
followUps: Estimate the probability of at least one failure.
